# taxify <img src="man/figures/logo.svg" align="right" height="139" alt="taxify logo" />

*species names matched to their accepted names, offline*

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/taxify)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=taxify)
[![CRAN downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/taxify)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=taxify)
[![Monthly downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/taxify)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=taxify)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/gcol33/taxify/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gcol33/taxify/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/gcol33/taxify/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/gcol33/taxify)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
<!-- badges: end -->

taxify matches taxonomic names, such as a field survey's species list or the species column of a trait table, to the name each taxon currently carries, its accepted name.

The package performs the name-resolution step of [taxize](https://docs.ropensci.org/taxize/) and [WorldFlora](https://cran.r-project.org/package=WorldFlora), run offline against local backbone files. A backbone is a published taxonomic database, such as the Catalogue of Life or World Flora Online, downloaded once and stored on your disk. Each name comes back with its accepted name, how it was matched, and the backbone version that matched it, so you can review the uncertain matches and decide which to keep. taxify supports:

- **Backbones for every group.** taxify reads <!-- manifest:backbone-count -->19<!-- /manifest:backbone-count --> taxon backbones: global checklists (Catalogue of Life, GBIF, ITIS, NCBI, Open Tree of Life) and the authorities of single groups (World Flora Online, WoRMS, Species Fungorum, AlgaeBase, FishBase, the Mammal Diversity Database, AviList and others), all returning the same columns. Several backbones form a fallback chain, so a name one backbone lacks is matched by the next.

- **Published data on the accepted name.** Trait, status and distribution datasets, <!-- manifest:enrichment-count -->109<!-- /manifest:enrichment-count --> of them, from the IUCN Red List to seed mass and fish morphology, are joined by the accepted name, so a dataset that writes a synonym still lines up. [`add_trait()`](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/reference/add_trait.html) gathers one trait from every dataset that carries it.

- **Checking a list.** [`inspect()`](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/reference/inspect.html) returns only the names that need a look (typos, outdated synonyms, spellings shared by several taxa, unknown genera, an animal in a plant list), each with the name to use.

- **Vegetation units.** Two vegetation classifications, the EuroVegChecklist and the Czech national classification, resolve alliance and association names the way species names are resolved.

The accepted name is the backbone's own, and where backbones disagree, `mode = "wide"` shows each one's answer side by side. Every row records the backbone and its version, `cite()` prints the references of every backbone and dataset a result used, and `taxify_lock()` saves the versions so the analysis can be rerun on the same data. A script in the repository matches 300 World Flora Online names in taxify and in WorldFlora; 277 get the same accepted name, and [Compatibility with taxize and WorldFlora](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/migration.html) shows where and why the others differ.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("taxify")

# or the development version
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/taxify")
```

`install_backbones()` downloads the Catalogue of Life (COL), the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy and the Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS), about 4 GB in all, and `taxify()` reads them from disk after that. `taxify_clean()` removes them again.

## Usage

1. Match the names with `taxify()`.

2. Look at the matches that need a decision with `inspect()`.

3. Join data on the accepted name with `add_data()` for your own table, or with an `add_<source>()` function for a published dataset.

```{r usage}
library(taxify)

names <- c("Quercus robur", "Quercus robus", "Pinus abies",
           "Fallopia japonica")
res <- taxify(names)
res[, c("input_name", "accepted_name", "match_type", "is_synonym")]
```

*Quercus robur* is matched as written. *Quercus robus* has a typo and reaches *Q. robur* by fuzzy matching, which compares it with the names of its own genus. *Pinus abies* and *Fallopia japonica* are outdated synonyms of *Picea abies* and *Reynoutria japonica*. The warning names an input whose spelling belongs to more than one accepted taxon; the `n_ids` and `accepted_ids` columns count and list them.

The input is a character vector of names. Authors, qualifiers such as `cf.` and `agg.`, capitals and an abbreviated genus are handled before matching. Without `backbone`, every installed backbone is tried in a fixed priority order, starting with the Catalogue of Life; `backbone = c("wfo", "col")` names the chain.

```{r inspect}
inspect(res)
```

`inspect()` labels each name with a tier: `review` for a match you have to decide on, `note` for a change you can accept. [Get started](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/taxify.html) follows a longer list to a table with traits attached.

## Joining data

`add_data()` matches the names of your own table against the same backbones and joins on the accepted name. Each published dataset has its own function, named after its source:

```r
res |> add_data("my_traits.csv")
res |> add_iucn() |> add_eive()
res |> add_trait("seed_mass")
```

`list_enrichments()` lists every published dataset with its version, size and source, and [Attaching published data](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/enrichments.html) shows the joins in full.

## Choosing backbones

Each backbone is downloaded once, as a file built by the companion package [taxifydb](https://github.com/gcol33/taxifydb), and pinned by version. A vector of backbones forms a fallback chain: every backbone is asked for an exact match before any is asked for a fuzzy one.

```r
taxify(names, backbone = c("wfo", "col"))
```

`list_backbones()` reports each backbone's scope, size, version and whether it is installed. [Choosing and combining backbones](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/backbones.html) covers the choice per group, downloads and version pinning, and [The backbones and datasets](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/databases.html) describes each one.

## Exploring the backbone

The backbone files also answer lookups by synonym, rank and lineage:

```r
synonyms("Picea abies")                     # every synonym of a name
children("Quercus")                         # the species of a genus
upstream("Quercus robur", to = "family")    # the family of a name
sci2comm("Quercus robur")                   # common names
parse_name("Quercus robur (L.) H.Karst.")   # genus, epithet, author
```

[Exploring the backbone](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/exploring.html) shows these and the other lookup functions.

## Large lists

Names are matched in C through [vectra](https://gillescolling.com/vectra/), the column-store package taxify reads its backbone files with. A fuzzy match compares a name only with the names of its own genus. [Matching large lists](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/large-scale.html) gives timings for lists up to 100,000 names.

## Documentation

Start with [Get started](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/taxify.html): one path from a messy list to accepted names with traits attached.

- [Choosing and combining backbones](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/backbones.html): which backbone for which group, fallback chains, versions.

- [Checking a name list](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/inspecting-names.html): every label of `inspect()`, and `reconcile()` for a checklist.

- [Matching within a region](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/regions.html): preferring the species that occur where the list was made.

- [Attaching published data](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/enrichments.html) and [Joining your own data](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/custom-data.html): the two kinds of join.

- [Exploring the backbone](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/exploring.html): synonyms, children, classification and common names.

- [Requesting GBIF data for a species list](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/gbif-requests.html): from matched names to an occurrence download.

- [Matching vegetation units](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/vegetation-units.html): alliances and associations against the EuroVegChecklist.

- [Matching large lists](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/large-scale.html): timings, memory, and long lists run in parts.

- [How names are matched](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/fuzzy-matching.html) and [Hybrids and aggregates](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/hybrids-and-aggregates.html): the matching rules in detail.

- [Compatibility with taxize and WorldFlora](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/migration.html): agreement with WorldFlora, function mapping and timings.

- [The backbones and datasets](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/articles/databases.html): every backbone and dataset with its version, licence and reference.

- [Full reference](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/reference/): every function, grouped by job.

## Getting help

Questions and bug reports go to the [GitHub issues](https://github.com/gcol33/taxify/issues). A bug report is easiest to act on with a small reproducible example, for instance made with [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/).

## Citation

```{r citation, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cit <- citation("taxify")
fence <- function(lang, x) cat("```", lang, "\n", paste(x, collapse = "\n\n"), "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
cat(attr(cit, "mheader"), "\n\n", sep = "")
fence("text", format(cit, style = "text"))
cat("BibTeX:\n\n")
fence("bibtex", format(cit, style = "bibtex"))
```

Download the citation as [BibTeX](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/taxify.bib) or [RIS](https://gillescolling.com/taxify/taxify.ris).
